subject: POC sprint synchronization: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering
messages:
From: Simon Grey <simon@cardiotech.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cardiotech.com, ops@cardiotech.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — environment gating & MAP alignment

Hi Evelyn / Jordan,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the team is excited to move to a short proof-of-concept. Before we lock dates, procurement and our infra leads asked for a single mutual action plan (MAP) that lists the exact gating items for environment readiness. Specifically we need: API key provisioning process, org/tenant creation steps, IP allowlist ranges for our firewall team, and VPC peering window requirements.

Can you provide a one-page MAP and a target timeline so we can confirm with our security and procurement partners?

I've attached our internal network requirements to give you context. If you can draft the MAP by Monday, procurement will start the SOW paperwork.

Appreciate it,
Simon
---
Simon Grey
Head of Infrastructure, CardioTech
simon@cardiotech.com

Attachment: cardiotech-network-requirements.pdf (PDF, 312KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Simon Grey <simon@cardiotech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@cardiotech.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — environment gating & MAP alignment

Simon — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the network doc. Attached is a concise MAP draft (v1.2) that maps the gating items to owners and target dates. High level:

- Org setup: we will provision a customer tenant in our staging cluster. Required inputs: preferred org name, billing contact (we can accept a placeholder until SOW is final). Owner: Marissa. ETA: 48 business hours after we receive the org name.
- API keys: we will create scoped API keys for the POC (read-only for monitoring, read-write for test writes). Owner: Evelyn (platform). ETA: keys issued the same day org is provisioned.
- IP allowlist: we need CardioTech to confirm the final egress ranges. We will accept allowlist entries at the /24 or specific IP level; if you prefer CIDR ranges, send them to ops@redwood.com. Owner: Jordan. ETA: allowlist configured within 4 hours of receiving ranges (during business hours).
- VPC peering: supported for dedicated/private pilots. For hosted MAP we offer a VPN tunnel + strict IP allowlist; for Dedicated we coordinate a peering window (typically 2–4 hour maintenance window). Owner: Jordan. ETA: schedule to be confirmed after you pick Dedicated vs Hosted fallback.

Next steps I propose:
1) CardioTech confirms org name + billing placeholder and sends final IP ranges by Monday 10am PT.
2) We provision the org and issue API keys (same day).
3) Jordan schedules a 2-hour peering/handshake window if you opt for Dedicated; otherwise we enable VPN and allowlist.

I've attached the MAP (redwood-map-v1.2.xlsx) and a short checklist. If procurement needs a DocuSign, Marissa can start that parallel.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-map-v1.2.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Simon Grey <simon@cardiotech.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ops@cardiotech.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — environment gating & MAP alignment

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from infra:

- VPC peering specifics: if you choose Dedicated, we need a /27 or larger subnet for the peering interface (we recommend /24 if you want fewer collisions). Preferred window: Tue 2027-05-18 22:00–02:00 PT (low-traffic). Please confirm availability.
- Firewall / NAT: We will originate egress from our cluster IPs; CardioTech should allow inbound from these ranges. I've pasted the proposed Redwood egress CIDRs into the attached MAP worksheet.
- API key scopes: For the POC we'll issue a time-bound key (30 days) with token rotation instructions. If you need longer-lived tokens, we can discuss in procurement.

Simon — can your ops team confirm whether a peering /24 is acceptable? If not, we can proceed with VPN + allowlist which requires less coordination but slightly higher latency.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
